mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport for each director, shareholder, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or notary public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate for each director and UBO from country of residence
Certificate of Good Standing for corporate vehicles (if any)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions list, the UN consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and EU consolidated list. Enhanced due diligence required for PEPs and for any connection to high-risk jurisdictions. Screening must be completed within 5 business days prior to notarization of the incorporation deed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Central Name Index (Zentralindex / Zefix) operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office, accessible online at www.zefix.ch
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be in French, German, Italian, or Romansh using Latin script. Non-Latin transliteration is not accepted. The name must be exclusive, truthful, and not misleading within Switzerland. It must end with a legal form suffix 'AG' (Aktiengesellschaft) or 'SA' (Société Anonyme) depending on language.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: AG / SA (as part of another trade name)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written appeal to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 30 days of the rejection notice. If rejected again, appeal to the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister, EHRA) within 30 days. The appeal should include the proposed name again and a legal justification. If the rejection is based upon infringement of third-party rights, the applicant may seek judicial civil remedy before the appropriate cantonal court, but this does not suspend the initial administrative refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for an Aktiengesellschaft. A physical registered office in Switzerland is required, where statutes may be inspected, legal notices can be served, and administrative authorities can reach the board of directors. For Swiss data privacy and IT regulatory compliance, an active physical office is expected for ISIC 6201 activities, even though a home office located in Switzerland may be acceptable provided the address is suitable for service and signposted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Quantified risk below 2% per year for a standard low-risk software development and website builder company. Physical inspections may occur upon suspicion of false registration, money laundering, or commercial substance deficiencies, or as part of a criminal, regulatory, or tax investigation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance fee (Zefix Central Index search and cantonal reservation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per cantonal fee schedule (typically CHF 50–100)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the articles of association and incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard AG incorporation (CHF 1,500–3,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization of foreign original documents (passport copies, police clearances, statutory declaration, corporate certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of document origin (e.g., Notary Public and Official Apostille Agencies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention per-document fee plus expediting agent fee (approx. USD 50 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of articles of association and foreign documents into an official Swiss language (German/French/Italian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing translation market rate (≈ USD 40 per page)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of incorporation bank account (Escrow / Fiduciary account) and capital deposit confirmation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank opening fee and confirmation of paid-in share capital (CHF 100,000 nominal, min CHF 25,000 paid-up) – fee range CHF 200–500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register registration fee (publicizing incorporation in Zefix and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce, SOGC)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and SOGC

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing and declaration fee (reporting of beneficial owners to the OUBO registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat statutory filing fee pursuant to Swiss UBO registry regulation (CHF 150–200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial AML/CFT compliance on-boarding and PEP-screening package (UBO pinning, background report, sanctions list watchlist)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Swiss-licensed fiduciary service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial substance readiness checklist and registered office correspondence fee for first year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), Articles 626-670 (formation, organization, and shareholder rights of the stock corporation), Article 628 (minimum capital), Article 631 (statutes), Article 635 (paid-up capital), Article 643 (incorporation declaration), Article 644 (commercial register application).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered seat; federal supervision by the Swiss Commercial Register Authority under the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation incorporating the Articles of Association (Statuten) together with the incorporation report and proof of capital contribution; thereafter file for Commercial Register entry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum aggregate nominal share capital CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid up prior to registration. Payment is made into a blocked escrow account in the company's name and released only upon production of Commercial Register registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the company under the name [Company Name] AG, seat in [Place], is hereby ratified; that the share subscriptions made by the initial shareholders as listed in the articles of association are approved; that the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000 has been duly deposited and credited to the company's blocked capital account; that the registered office of the company is fixed at [Street Number], [Postal Code], [Place] as stated in Article 1 of the articles; that the Board of Directors is constituted; that [Name] is appointed as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Managing Director, each with signatory power per the signatory rules; and that the Board authorizes the Managing Director to effectuate all filings and registrations with the Commercial Register and the competent authorities for the purpose of completing incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via official online portal (e.g., EasyGov or cantonal platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name reservation application via the cantonal commercial register's online portal. Annotate the proposed corporate name, the legal form 'AG', and the purpose. After reservation, draft the notarial instrument and articles of association with legal counsel, ensuring compliance with OR Art. 626 et seq.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is not accepted or conflicts with existing trademarks, file a revised application with an alternative name; no additional fee if corrected within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Authentication of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public notary office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered seat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Schedule and attend appointment with a Swiss public notary. The notary verifies the share capital, subscribes to the assignments, announces the contents of the articles, and authenticates the founders' signatures. After notarization, the deed is legally effective and may be filed in the commercials register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notary issues a request for clarification, provide supplementary evidence (e.g., corrected articles) and resubmit; remedy within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Escrow Account and Paying Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank (retail or private bank) or licensed financial intermediary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Swiss bank account in the company name and deposit the minimum paid-up capital (CHF 50,000) into a blocked escrow account subject to a blocking instruction. The bank will provide a written confirmation (AMAS blockage declaration) to the commercial register. Funds remain blocked until the registration certificate is produced.
required_dossiers: Extract of commercial register (or draft deed)
Resolution or authorisation letter from founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries source of funds, supply bank statements within two weeks; if the bank rejects, choose another licensed bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed of incorporation, bank capital confirmation, and consent of directors via the electronic filing portal (EasyGov). The register reviews legal compliance and issues the Commercial Register entry. After entry, the formation is published in the Swiss Official Gazette (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Application form signed by all board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If objection/warning is raised, file concise rectification within 10 days addressing legal deficiencies; legal remedies lie with the competent commercial register supervisory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax ID, UID, and Employer Registration Post-Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Office (for UID and tax), Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) (VAT), and Compensation Fund (AHV/SUVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Commercial Register excerpt, apply for the Swiss Business Identification Number (UID) automatically assigned; register for VAT if annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or mandatory under national law; register as employer with the social security compensation fund and accident insurer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is contested, file a declaration with the relevant authority; administrative delays may be cured by submitting written form and confirmation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None – software/online service operation is not an industrial activity; no industrial operating permit is required under the Swiss Federal Act on Work on the Employment of Workers (ArG) or the Swiss Ordinance on Industrial Licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – general commercial activity subject only to registration and tax permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) / Cantonal Environmental Protection Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based, no production facility, digital service provider (ISIC 6201) falls outside the scope of the EIA Ordinance (UVPV).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No applicable discharge or emission thresholds; activities generate no point-source pollution; general waste and e-waste handling per federal technical ordnance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and building clearance per the cantonal building insurance and fire prevention authority; an occupancy permit from the municipal building inspectorate is required for employee-occupied offices; occupational workplace safety inspection per SUVA accident prevention guidelines; worktime and welfare compliance under ArG.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV/FTA), VAT Division; official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; e-services via SuisseTax and www.uid.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity (CH_AG) must file VAT registration with ESTV before performing taxable Swiss supplies. If annual turnover in Switzerland exceeds CHF 100,000, registration is compulsory. For foreign suppliers with no Swiss establishment, a Swiss fiscal representative is required, except for the simplified e-commerce procedure (quick registration). Required documents: certificate of incorporation, statutory seat, business description, expected Swiss turnover, and authorization letter. ESTV assigns the Swiss UID (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) and VAT registration number; processing time 10–25 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss tax law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid branch classification elections. A Swiss AG is mandatorily taxed as a separate legal entity; no pass-through status is possible. Available optional regimes include election for simplified VAT net-taxation method (for groups), voluntary VAT registration below the threshold, participation relief election, and group capital tax relief. For hybrid mismatches, Switzerland applies mandatory BEPS/ATAD-compliant rules without elective departure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer) - national VAT administered by the ESTV
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover sourced in Switzerland (Art. 10/11 MWSTG); for foreign digital service suppliers, the same threshold applies; below it registration is optional but can be elected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic clearing or fiscal stamp. Switzerland uses the Swiss QR-Bill for paper and electronic invoices; invoices for taxable supplies must include VAT details. B2G e-invoicing adopts Peppol/B2G via eBill (since 2020) for federal procurement. All VAT-relevant records must be retained in an audit-proof electronic format for 10 years; no fiscal API clearance is currently imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To apply 0% VAT on exports of goods or offshore services, the AG must prove (1) for goods: physical removal from Switzerland to a foreign destination evidenced by customs declarations and transport documents; (2) for services: the recipient is a foreign business with no Swiss seat, and the service is supplied to that business under B2B place-of-supply rules; specifically, digital/intangible services are Swiss-exempt if the business customer is abroad. Documentation must be in place at the time of goods/service supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (LAD/e-dec/ERIKA) with a customs officer stamp or electronic release
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR (proving physical export)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer confirmation (SWIFT MT103) showing payment from the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice and contract with the foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export documentation is incomplete or false, the ESTV retrospectively assesses VAT at the standard rate for the year, plus default interest of 5% p.a. (tax claim period: 10 years). Administrative fines under Art. 69/70 MWSTG amount up to 100% of the evaded VAT; intentional forgery of export evidence triggers criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to CHF 500,000. The AG may also be barred from the simplified export invoice procedure for up to 3 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Schweizerische Nationalbank (SNB / Swiss National Bank), acting under the National Bank Act of 2003 (NBA), the Federal Act on the Free Movement of Capital (FMCA), and the Foreign Exchange and Payment Transactions Ordinance; the SNB is the sole monetary authority, while bank licensing and prudential supervision are conducted by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland imposes no exchange-control regime; the CHF is freely convertible on both capital and current account with full cross-border capital mobility guaranteed under the FMCA, and no prior authorisation, repatriation, or compulsory conversion requirements apply. Profit remittance is governed solely by corporate solvency rules under the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO Art. 660) and by a 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends, which is fully refundable to Swiss residents and generally reduced to 0% under the Swiss-EU or relevant tax treaties for qualified foreign recipients; no SNB approval or central-bank-level remittance consent is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law and SNB regulations neither prescribe a statutory surrender timeline nor a mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; an exported SaaS subscription revenue may be retained indefinitely in any currency (CHF, USD, EUR) in domestic or foreign bank accounts, subject only to AMLA documentation, FINMA circular 2023/1 ‘Statutory auditor AML duties’ at the bank level and SNB statistical reporting on cross-border payments for balance-of-payments compilation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary treasury rails, Low for primary banking. FINMA-licensed fintech companies under Art. 1b Banking Act may hold public deposits up to CHF 100 million and offer digital regulated accounts with Swiss IBANs; however, full e-money issuance requires a FINMA banking or fintech licence, and foreign EMIs (e.g., UK or Lithuanian EMI licence holders) are not passportable into Switzerland unless authorisation transfer are impossible, so offshore digital EMIs can only be used for FX conversion or distribution-side collection, not as the main corporate settlement account. The target rails (Stripe Billing, Paddle) should settle directly or via a cascade into a tier-1 Swiss bank account; fintech EMIs may act as merchant-of-record payment sub-accounts subject to FINMA outsourcing rules and bank-substitute risk limits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical visit to the bank is generally required for the authorised signatory/s unless the bank participates in FINMA-recognised video-identification (eID) procedures; when all directors are non-resident, tier-1 banks in practice impose at least one physical onboarding meeting in Switzerland or a meeting at a Swiss embassy/consulate with a notarised POA, and the AG must maintain a registered office and demonstrable substance in Switzerland (registered address, direct phone line, local corporate mailbox, administrative support). Remote opening of a CHF multi-currency treasury account is therefore possible only with a Swiss-based authorised director or a recognised Swiss fiduciary representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the commercial register purpose (software development) and the effective no-code website-builder activity conducted predominantly cross-border.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Handelsregister excerpt (not older than 30 days), updated Articles of Association (Statuten) expressly covering software development, SaaS, platform provision and related services; a board resolution approving the bank onboarding and confirming the effective business model; IT service agreements and a business plan; Swiss VAT registration certificate (MWST) and, where applicable, the audit-exempt declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or beneficial owners from multiple jurisdictions, increasing unexplained-wealth and tax-transparency scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports with sworn/notarised translations to German/English, proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement within 3 months), tax residence certificates (Form 85/Form A for Swiss tax, or CRS forms for foreign residents), CVs, professional references, source-of-wealth documentation, and a clear UBO organigram with the full AG shareholding chain certified by a licensed fiduciary (Treuhänder).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Association of the Zug ‘Crypto Valley’ domicile with digital-asset activities, even though the entity performs no custody, exchange, or financial-intermediation functions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written legal opinion from a Swiss law firm confirming absence of FINMA licensable activity and no obligation to join a self-regulatory organisation (SRO) under the AMLA; a board declaration that the company does not handle client funds, does not control digital wallets, and does not accept virtual currencies; the platform’s terms of use and payment-processing agreements demonstrating that Stripe and Paddle act as independent payment providers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS revenue with a high volume of low-value B2B/B2C transactions routed via payment gateways, creating fragmented transaction records and sanctions-screening gaps.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full payment-processor agreements (Stripe, Paddle), a monthly transaction reconciliation report with volume/threshold analysis, automated sanctions screening logs (OFAC, EU, SECO lists), evidence of geo-blocking where required, data-flow diagrams, and an internal AML risk assessment confirming a low-risk rating under the ODA-FINMA guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The no-code platform could be misused by end clients for phishing sites, fraudulent storefronts, or illicit content, posing reputational and anti-money-laundering risks to the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive Acceptable-Use Policy and abuse-handling procedure, content-moderation/DMCA takedown protocol, blacklisting mechanisms, domain-safety reporting, cooperation commitments with Swiss law enforcement (including SECO, fedpol and the Cybercrime Coordination Unit Switzerland CYCO), and a deposition that the company processes only the user-generated content that is legally attributable to its customers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial CHF 100,000 statutory minimum capital (Art. 621 CO, CHF 50,000 must be paid in immediately) must be wired via SIC (CHF) or SEPA/SWIFT MT103 (EUR/USD) from the shareholders' bank account to the AG’s capital escrow account using SWIFT field 70 purpose code 'Kapitaleinlage / Contribution to share capital' plus reference to the deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde). The bank will require the notarial deed, the subscribed capital statement, and the confirmation by the licensed auditor (for mandatory audits) or the board in the audit-exemption declaration; the funds must be credited to a blocked or earmarked account referenced to the commercial register application, and the capital contribution must be posted separately in the capital contribution reserve (Reserven aus Kapitaleinlagen / KER) ledger to preserve qualification for tax-free repayment under Swiss withholding-tax law. For foreign currency injection converted to CHF, the conversion must be executed at an onshore bank-quoted exchange rate, and the paying bank must complete the customer-due-diligence documentation; no SNB reporting or licence is required for capital import.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for the SaaS (cloud infrastructure, marketing services, affiliate commissions, software licensing, personnel) shall be executed through SIC/SIC Instant for CHF, SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR, or SWIFT MT103 (with mandatory UETR) for USD and other currencies. The recommended clearing rails: (i) corporate online-banking SWIFT MT103 with field 70 business-purpose codes for all non-SEPA payments, (ii) commercial letters of credit (UCP600, usually not required for software services but available for future hardware resale), (iii) escrow-backed milestone settlements for large platform-integration engagements, and (iv) direct-debit/QR-bill for Swiss domestic counterparties. To avoid dual FX conversion, the account must be configured as a multi-currency treasury account allowing native settlement of USD (via Fedwire/CHIPS through the bank's New York correspondent), EUR (via Target2), and CHF (SIC); SNB regulations do not require export proceeds to be brought onshore, but adequate cash-pooling and 13-26 week cash-flow forecasting must be documented for the bank’s periodic reviews.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (custom USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, GBP/CHF contracts up to 24 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or Swiss Master Agreement; economically covering SaaS subscription revenues and cloud-infrastructure costs)
FX Swaps (swap of principal and interest in diff currencies for intercompany liquidity management)
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) for long-term hedging of capital injections or acquisition financing
FX Options (vanilla European-style options, including collars and zero-cost structures, for asymmetric protection on USD/CHF and EUR/CHF exposure)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to secondary emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) where local convertibility restrictions prevent deliverable hedging; CHF/ EUR / USD NDFs are generally unavailable because CHF is a fully deliverable currency with a deep onshore forward market, and any synthetic products must comply with FINMA market-rules and hold-adequacy requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements at the ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (AGM), including the appropriation of profit and the discharge (décharge) of the board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate organ — General Meeting of Shareholders; the approved statements are retained in the corporate dossier and submitted only upon request to the statutory auditor, tax authorities, or creditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year end (Art. 699(4) Swiss Code of Obligations); for a calendar-year stock company, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Personal liability of directors for proven damages (Art. 754 CO); any shareholder representing 10% of voting rights may petition the court to convene an AGM; failure does not attract an administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined cantonal and federal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen) and associated protective/status declarations for the annual assessment period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered seat (e.g., Steueramt des Kantons Zug) acting for the combined cantonal and direct federal tax assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The canton sets a filing season for the preceding tax year that generally expires on 31 March; routine extensions to 30 June and, on justified request, 30 September are accepted in most cantons; interim prepayments are invoiced in spring and late summer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default interest on arrears, estimated assessment by the tax authority where no return is filed, procedural fines for non-cooperation (up to CHF 10,000 under the Federal Direct Tax Act), and criminal evasion penalties up to roughly three times the evaded tax under the revised penalty regime; does not trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT reconciliation — final quarter and year-end settlement return in the Swiss e-Decl system, including input VAT recovery and OSS-type digital services declarations applicable to software sales of the no-code website builder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Authority — Swiss VAT Division (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: VAT accounting period equals the calendar year; quarterly returns are due within 60 days of the quarter end, so the fourth-quarter return constitutes the annual settlement and is filed by roughly 1 March of the following year unless a monthly, semiannual, or annual filing mode has been granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid VAT, enforcement through debt collection, procedural fines and penal orders under the Swiss VAT Act, and refusal of input VAT deduction in serious non-compliance cases; no effect on the commercial register status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Structural Business Survey — compulsory annual enterprise questionnaire for the software and computer-programming sector (ISIC 6201) aligned with the Swiss Business and Enterprise Register (BUR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (Bundesamt für Statistik, BFS), coordinated with the cantonal statistical office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The online questionnaire is dispatched in January–February each year and must generally be returned within 30 days of receipt of the access credentials for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine under the Federal Statistics Act for refusal or repeated delay in supplying mandatory survey data — in practice a warning followed by modest monetary fines; no administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner transparency register (Transparenzregister) — event-driven UBO update coinciding with the annual corporate secretarial review and any shareholding transfer during the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Office of Police (fedpol) — Transparency Register; filed electronically via the official Transparenzregister portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No standalone annual form; initial registration was due within one year of the register's operational go-live of 4 October 2023, and every change in a natural person's qualifying interest of 25% or more (or controlling influence) must be reported within 30 days; an annual register-accuracy sign-off is recommended to coincide with the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and penal consequences under Articles 49i–49j of the Anti-Money Laundering Act for late, omitted, or false beneficial-owner declarations; does not trigger commercial register strike-off but heightens bank and AML compliance risk for the entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A full statutory audit (ordentliche Revision) is mandatory when any two of the three following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million, turnover above CHF 40 million, or average annual headcount above 250 full-time equivalents (Art. 727 CO). All other stock companies require at least a limited audit (eingeschränkte Revision); audit opting-out is available only if the company employs on average 10 full-time equivalents or fewer and every shareholder consents annually in writing — a shareholder holding 10% of the share capital may nevertheless demand a limited audit (Art. 727a CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and notes) are prepared in accordance with the Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–963b CO); a larger or listed entity may voluntarily apply IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER as a permissible elevated framework. The no-code software AG must recognize recurring subscription revenue consistently, capitalize qualifying platform development costs, and file withholding-tax declarations on distributions and board fees.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For shareholding transfers, the board must enter the new owner in the share register (Aktienbuch) before voting rights can be exercised, and any beneficial owner with a qualifying interest of 25% or more must be mirrored in fedpol's Transparenzregister within 30 days of the change (Art. 49a–49k AMLA). There is no separate annual UBO return; however, the corporate secretarial calendar requires an end-of-year integrity review of the register, AGM sign-off confirming no unreported ownership movement, and annual updating of know-your-customer files for the payment rails (Stripe and Paddle) and banking partners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (protocols of board and general-meeting resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,400 – 3,200 per year for a Swiss corporate-services and registered-office provider in Zug or Zurich bundling registered-address services, commercial-register correspondence, UID maintenance, AGM administration, and statutory-secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 – 3,600 for an audit opt-out confirmation or statutory limited-review file for a small software AG; USD 4,500 – 9,000 for a full statutory audit where thresholds are approached or a shareholder requires ordentliche Revision.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct profit tax on net income after tax (equivalent to 7.83% taxable-base pre-tax); plus cantonal/communal profit tax, typically 11.5%-21% aggregate ordinary rate depending on corporate seat (e.g., Zug aggregate 11.9%, Geneva aggregate 21%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory federal tax holiday. Federal profit tax is 8.5% post-tax; cantonal incentives include patent box exemption for qualifying IP income (up to 90% exempt, remaining 10% taxed), research and development super deduction up to 150% of eligible Swiss R&D costs, and notional interest deduction on taxed paid-in capital. Combined effective Swiss tax rate for a digital-royalty company with qualifying IP can be reduced to approximately 7%-9% after incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss direct tax return forms for corporations: 'Formulaire pour personnes morales / Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Formulario per persone giuridiche' (combined federal, cantonal, and communal tax return); electronic submission via Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA/AFC) supported software in most cantons, including SuisseTax, VaudTax, ZUGTax Online, and related cantonal e-portals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return is due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; this period is automatically extended in most cantons to no later than 9 months after year-end for tax-authorised advisors, and at the discretion of the cantonal authority to 12 months. If no return is submitted, the cantonal and federal tax authorities issue an ex officio assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross worldwide revenue from web-template subscriptions, low-code plans, software licences, and support fees; reduce chargebacks and refunds; disclose deferred revenue netting and performance obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident AG: report gross Swiss-sourced revenue only if a generating Swiss permanent establishment (PE) exists. Without a PE, service revenue belongs to the registered office and is reported in the country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs: cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure), CDN, domain names, payment processor fees (Stripe/Paddle), software development salaries, marketing, legal fees, and rent. Only arm's-length and documented expenses are deductible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: allocate expenses to the Swiss PE on a functionally separate basis; head-office charges and intra-group royalties must satisfy OECD transfer-pricing and substance requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual taxable profit after depreciation, amortisation, loss carry-forward, and elimination of non-deductible hidden profit distributions and capital taxes. The federal tax base is then multiplied by the 7.83% factor to impose the 8.5% post-tax federal rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: include only Swiss PE-attributable profit; no apportionment of worldwide income except in the absence of separate accounting under the relevant tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 (Taxable equity for cantonal capital tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Paid-in share capital, statutory reserves, retained earnings, and adjustments for the cantonal capital levy. A low-code AG with the statutory minimum CHF 100,000 fully paid-in share capital must declare deductible net equity after tax-privileged participating interests.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation without a Swiss PE is not subject to cantonal capital tax; if a Swiss branch is registered, branch net equity must be declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualified Swiss R&D labour costs and the 150% super deduction; the deduction applies to software-engineering and copyrightable code development performed by Swiss staff or contractors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: claim only if the Swiss PE performs the R&D activity; foreign R&D costs are not eligible for the Swiss super deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income from qualifying IP rights, including software copyright-protected code and patent-protected UI components, exempt at cantonal/communal level; the residual 10% remains taxable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: not available for IP not held in a Swiss PE; the cantonal tax administration can require a licence-substantiation file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year losses up to seven years. Related-party change of control may extinguish the loss carry-forward where economic identity has ceased.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: cannot offset foreign company losses against Swiss PE income unless the PE is the same taxpayer and the losses were incurred in the Swiss assessment unit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return: procedural fine up to CHF 1,000 plus legal interest surcharge of 3.5% per annum on the unpaid assessment. Repeated non-filing triggers ex officio assessment with a mandatory procedural penalty of 0.25% of assessed tax per month, minimum CHF 50. Deliberately false returns constitute tax evasion and attract a criminal fine of up to twice the evaded federal tax, minimum CHF 1,000; qualified fraud with forged books can lead to imprisonment up to 3 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on cash dividends, bonus shares, hidden profit distributions, and profits remitted by the Aktiengesellschaft to shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced Swiss DTA rate, the foreign shareholder must submit a refund/exemption application to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration using the prescribed forms, generally Form 823A for partial refund after payment and Form 822A for exemption at source, together with a valid residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. Supporting evidence of beneficial ownership, shareholding percentage, and holding period must be attached. Most Swiss DTAs reduce dividend withholding tax to 0-5% for shareholdings of at least 10%, subject to the treaty-specific 6-month or 1-year holding condition, and 5-15% for portfolio shares. Refund applications must be filed within three years after the calendar year of tax withholding. A principal-purpose test or limitation-on-benefits analysis is necessary to avoid treaty-shopping denial.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss withholding tax does not apply to royalties for the use of software copyright, know-how, or arm's-length loan interest, unless the interest is paid on Swiss bond-like instruments or profit-sharing loans. Under most Swiss DTAs, interest is taxable only in the residence state or capped at a 5% source rate, and royalties are usually taxable only in the state of the beneficial owner. If a reduced treaty rate applies, the same TRC and Form 823A/822A protocol is used because there is no general 35% Swiss withholding tax on such royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Swiss Local File is expected where aggregate cross-border transactions between the AG and related parties exceed CHF 1,000,000 per fiscal year; a Master File should accompany groups with consolidated revenue above CHF 1 billion and related-party cross-border transactions exceeding CHF 1,000,000. Documentation must be contemporaneous, prepared in German, French, Italian, or English, and filed with the cantonal tax administration upon request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no offshore-style standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR), but the economic-substance doctrine is applied through Swiss case law on actual management, tax treaty anti-abuse rules, and OECD BEPS. A Zug-registered AG that merely holds a no-code website builder brand, earns licence fees, and has all operational functions performed from a foreign affiliate will be treated as an artificial arrangement and denied treaty benefits, participation exemption, and withholding tax relief. Core business functions, strategic decision-making, personnel, premises, and CRM/payment-support activity must be documented in Switzerland to substantiate the commercial seat.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-reporting revenue earned from Stripe, Paddle, or direct website-subscription sales; posting false deferred-revenue schedules; concealing Swiss bank accounts or crypto exchange balances related to the low-code website builder; suppressing pre-payments and licence contracts to reduce federal and cantonal profit tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax evasion: fine of up to twice the amount of federal tax evaded, never less than CHF 1,000; legal interest of 3.5% per annum on the back tax. Qualified tax fraud with falsified books carries a custodial sentence of up to 3 years or a monetary penalty under the Direct Federal Tax Act and cantonal direct-tax laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for the AG's tax debt, but a director who signs, prepares, or orders a false return may be personally fined and exposed to civil restitution under Art. 754 Code of Obligations for fiscal damage. Criminal prosecution can trigger asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Swiss Criminal Code for fraud or related offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Zug mailbox AG with no employees, no director meetings in Switzerland, all decision-making outsourced to a foreign affiliate, and no substantive commercial IT support for the No-Code Website Builder; charging above-market royalties or inflated cost-plus margins to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as an abusive arrangement: disallowance of intercompany deductions, upward transfer-pricing adjustment, Swiss corporate tax on diverted profits, and withholding tax at 35% on deemed hidden profit distributions under Art. 20 Swiss Withholding Tax Act. Treaty relief is denied, and cantonal procedural penalties apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For an insolvent shell AG, directors can be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they failed to preserve statutory accounts, file insolvency notification, or maintain true share capital. A director who organises an artificial arrangement may face criminal conviction for fraud in tax collection, asset seizure, travel bans, and extradition under mutual legal assistance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a de facto payment intermediary without Swiss AML or FinIA authorisation, including holding customer settlement funds, managing merchant onboarding, or controlling residual payout balances. Using Paddle or Stripe as a merchant of record normally shields the AG, but the AG becomes a regulated financial intermediary if it controls inbound fund flows or acquirer relationships.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative enforcement by FINMA: prohibition of business activity, disgorgement of profits, and penalties up to CHF 500,000 for negligent violation of FinIA/FinSA. Knowingly laundering proceeds under Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code carries custodial sentence up to 3 years, or up to 5 years for qualified laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to FINMA enforcement as natural persons in serious cases, and criminal liability under Art. 305bis/306 SCG can trigger pre-trial detention, asset freezing, Interpol notices, travel restrictions, and civil liability to merchants and customers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and retain a contemporaneous Swiss Local File or Master File for related-party licence agreements with the offshore sales entity, or setting a royalty, trademark, or technical service fee outside the arm's-length range without a functional and risk analysis for the ISIC 6201 business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment by tax authorities under the OECD TNMM, CUP, or Profit Split benchmarks; upward profit adjustment; 35% withholding tax on recharacterised hidden distributions; late-payment interest at 3.5% per annum; and procedural penalties for lack of documentation up to CHF 10,000 at the cantonal level.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly omits required documentation or instructs transfer-pricing analysts to fabricate comparables can be prosecuted under Swiss administrative tax penalty law. In insolvency, civil restitution claims survive, and managing directors may face travel bans while administrative proceedings are pending.
